newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo tourism down 6.5 pct in Jan-Nov - statistics.
newsitem.headline: Yugo tourism down 6.5 pct in Jan-Nov - statistics.

text.p: Yugoslavia registered a total of 2.7 million tourists from January to November 1996, or 6.5 percent less than in the same period 1995, the Federal Statistics Office said on Thursday.
Yugoslavs accounted for 2.41 million of the total, down 10 percent on the same period 1995.
Little more than 152,000 foreigners visited the country over the period, the report said.
The greatest number of foreign visitors, 17,759, came from the Russian Federation, followed by 16,503 from Italy, 12,286 from Greece, 11,581 from Bulgaria and 11,165 from Germany.
The number of tourists from other republics of former Yugoslavia -- Bosnia, Croatia, Macedonia and Slovenia -- rose to 130,756 from 120,794.

According to National Bank of Yugoslavia data, hard currency income from tourism in the January-October period stood at $35.4 million, unchanged on the same period 1996. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
